title: Which two numbers come next in this pattern?
description: A pattern of decimals changes in turns. The first changes are found by taking one number from the next, the turns are followed to write the next two numbers, and the answer is checked against the turns.
teaching_notes: One idea: when changes take turns, find both changes and follow the turns to the next numbers. Watch for students who repeat the last change instead of the next one in the turns.

source: Figure it Out (end of chapter), Q10
video_script.why: The child can find a single change and continue a pattern, and now meets a pattern whose changes take turns.
video_script.substitution: Find the first two changes, see that they take turns, and follow the turns to the next numbers.
video_script.anchor: A pattern of decimals that is missing its last two numbers.
video_script.payoff_line: Follow the turns of the changes, add then take away

final_answer.spoken: nine point zero seven and nine point zero six

maths_rules: 6.4 - 5.5 = 0.9, so the first change is add 0.9
6.4 - 6.39 = 0.01, so the next change is take away 0.01
7.29 - 6.39 = 0.9 and 7.29 - 7.28 = 0.01, so the changes take turns
the last change shown is take away 0.01 (8.18 to 8.17), so add 0.9 next: 8.17 + 0.9 = 9.07
video_script.design: The seven numbers sit in a row with arrows between them, alternating up and down, and two empty boxes at the end. The next arrow is chosen from the turns and each box fills in.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a pattern of decimals.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The numbers are five point five, six point four and six point three nine.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Then seven point two nine, seven point two eight and eight point one eight.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last number shown is eight point one seven.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What two numbers come next?

beats.on_screen: the row stays on the board with the two empty boxes

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.colours: the up arrow in one colour, the down arrow in another
narration: <bookmark mark='turns'/>A pattern can have two changes that take turns.
<bookmark mark='kind'/>One change may be an add, and the other a take away.
<bookmark mark='follow'/>We follow the turns to find the next numbers.
<bookmark mark='g1'/>Given, the pattern starts five point five, six point four, six point three nine.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>It goes on with seven point two nine and seven point two eight.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>Then eight point one eight and eight point one seven.

marks.b: 6.4 - 6.39 = 0.01 is written, with a down arrow

beats.colours: up arrow in one colour, down arrow in another
narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, find the first two changes.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Six point four take away five point five is zero point nine.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Six point four take away six point three nine is zero point zero one.

marks.rule: the words check the next changes are written
marks.a: 7.29 - 6.39 = 0.9 is written, with an up arrow
marks.b: 7.29 - 7.28 = 0.01 is written, with a down arrow
marks.turns: add 0.9, then take away 0.01 is written under the arrows

beats.colours: up arrow in one colour, down arrow in another
narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, check the next two changes.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Seven point two nine take away six point three nine is zero point nine.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Seven point two nine take away seven point two eight is zero point zero one.
<bookmark mark='turns'/>The changes take turns, add zero point nine, then take away zero point zero one.

beats.on_screen: last change shown 8.18 to 8.17 is take away, so add 0.9 next: tenths 1 + 9 = 10, write 0 carry 1; units 8 + 1 = 9; 8.17 + 0.9 = 9.07

marks.rule: the last arrow, 8.18 to 8.17, is marked take away and the next arrow is marked add
marks.t: tenths 1 + 9 = 10 is written, 0 below and 1 carried
marks.u: units 8 + 1 = 9 is written, with the hundredths 7 below
marks.sum: 8.17 + 0.9 = 9.07 is written in the first empty box

beats.colours: the carried digit in a new colour
beats.moves_through: one ten moves left as a carry
narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step three, the last change shown is a take away, so an add comes next.
<bookmark mark='t'/>Tenths: one plus nine is ten, so write zero and carry one.
<bookmark mark='u'/>Units: eight plus one is nine, and the hundredths stay seven.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>That is nine point zero seven.

beats.on_screen: a take away comes after an add: hundredths 7 - 1 = 6; 9.07 - 0.01 = 9.06

marks.rule: the next arrow is marked take away
marks.diff: 9.07 - 0.01 = 9.06 is written in the second empty box

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step four, a take away comes after an add.
<bookmark mark='h'/>Hundredths: seven take away one is six.
<bookmark mark='diff'/>Nine point zero seven take away zero point zero one is nine point zero six.

marks.check: the words check the two new numbers are written
marks.a: 9.07 - 8.17 = 0.9 is written and matches the add
marks.b: 9.07 - 9.06 = 0.01 is written and matches the take away
marks.hold: a tick is placed beside both

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check the two new numbers against the turns.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Nine point zero seven take away eight point one seven is zero point nine.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Nine point zero seven take away nine point zero six is zero point zero one.
<bookmark mark='hold'/>Add, then take away, so the turns hold.

marks.payoff: the rule is written above the answer
marks.ans: the two boxes are boxed as the answer

narration: <bookmark mark='payoff'/>Follow the turns of the changes, add then take away.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The next two numbers are nine point zero seven and nine point zero six.
